items.title: A solution of bounded dynamic range yields a linearly ordered colouring with logarithmically many colours
items.author: Johan Hastad; Bjorn Martinsson; Tamio-Vesa Nakajima; Stanislav Zivny
items.work: A logarithmic approximation of linearly ordered colourings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 266-271: if a homogeneous system has a solution whose largest absolute coordinate value is M and whose smallest positive absolute value is m, then the associated hypergraph has a linearly ordered colouring with two plus the logarithm to base two of the ratio of M to m colours. The proof (source lines 273-288) changes the shape of the requirement first, asking that the minimum colour in each edge be unique and reversing the colour order at the end, which is only legitimate because the reversal preserves the property; it then assigns colours according to which dyadic interval a coordinate falls into, separately for positive and negative coordinates, and the verification of uniqueness is where the ratio of the extreme absolute values is converted into the number of colours. The statement records the colour count and none of the normalisation or the construction.

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled lemma, retained line for line
